Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage ... try again at 5:41 PM.` — no refutations were produced by gpt-5.6-sol, so the whole review below is this model's own, against the same target list)

findings.what: D15's intent-derived op key makes UNMATCH-then-REMATCH a silent no-op: the second submission replays the voided match's receipt, the face renders the persistent 'no new cash entry was created' outcome naming a match that no longer exists, and the line stays unmatched.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_657 with a throwaway cell (packages/db/tests/zz-adv657-throwaway.test.mjs, run then deleted), real `humanQuery` persona, one fixed op key standing in for the pure function the web computes. (1) match line->entry 55_000 under key K => {"status":"live","match_id":"ed87ea95-fc26-4726-84e0-bff863c1825b","new_journal_entries":0,...}. (2) unmatch_bank_match(match_id) => the line is back on list_unmatched_lines (printed `true`). (3) resubmit the IDENTICAL intent under the SAME key => ok:true, payload BYTE-IDENTICAL, `second.match_id === first.match_id` => true. (4) `select count(*) from clara.bank_matches where client_id=$1 and status in ('pending','live')` => 0 rows. (5) list_unmatched_lines still contains the line => true. The mechanism: _reserve_op (0004_governed_fns.sql:50-58) keys only on (firm_id, fn, op_key) and returns the stored `result` whenever the request hash agrees; it knows nothing about whether the match it describes is still live. The web key is a PURE function of {client, sorted lineIds, sorted entries+cents, ack} (match-opkey.ts:49-63, 91-96), so the two submissions are identical by construction. The renewal rule at match-opkey.ts:6-10 enumerates what renews the key and an unmatch is not on the list. The path is reachable from ONE surface: unmatchBankMatch is wired into the same MatchingSection (apps/web/components/bank/matching-section.tsx:225), and #671 owns resolve-then-match on top of this chassis. The user-visible lie is matching-outcome.tsx:60-64 (`outcomeNoNewCash` from `receipt.new_journal_entries`) and :63-64 (`receipt.match_id`), both fed the replayed payload. Before this branch, match-doors.ts minted `crypto.randomUUID()` per call, so this could not happen — it is a regression introduced by D15, not a pre-existing hole.
findings.fix: Fold a data-derived generation into the intent tuple so the key renews when the WORLD changes, preserving D15's 'property of the data, not of a lifecycle'. The cheapest one is already on the wire after 0226: add each selected entry's `match_history.length` (or the newest `match_history[0].match_id`) from the recut list_bank_match_candidates row to `canonicalMatchIntent`. An unmatch appends to that entry's history, so the re-decision hashes differently while a lost response / re-render / reload does not. Add a DB cell in bank-line-existing-booking.test.mjs that matches, unmatches, replays the same key and asserts the second call does NOT return a live receipt, and a web cell `p657.web.opkey-renews-after-unmatch`.

findings.what: `candidate_basis` is one row per APPROVED BANK-TOUCHING ENTRY, not one row per candidate: it omits the `debit_remaining_cents > 0 or credit_remaining_cents > 0` filter the candidate read applies, so it is an unbounded superset that includes entries the surface can never offer.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_657 (same throwaway cell). R2: one entry's whole 77_000 capacity burned, then `list_bank_match_candidates` => 2 rows and `get_bank_line_matching_context(...)->'candidate_basis'` => 3 rows; `spent entry present in candidates? false -- present in basis? true`; the extra basis row reads {"entry_id":"e681522f-...","amount_exact":false,"date_delta_days":49,"counterparty_match":"none","class_hint":"other"}. R5 on a client seeded to 15 approved bank-touching entries: `candidate_basis rows: 15 | candidates: 13 | approved bank-touching entries: 15` — the basis tracks the ENTRY count exactly, the candidate count not at all. In source: the candidate read wraps its projection in `) t where (t.row_j->>'debit_remaining_cents')::bigint > 0 or (t.row_j->>'credit_remaining_cents')::bigint > 0` (0226:352-353); the basis subquery ends at `) b;` (0226:627) with no such filter and no LIMIT. This contradicts the migration's own comment at :568 ('one row per candidate entry of this line's bank account'), the function comment at :669, brief-657.md §3 item 3 ('one deterministic row per candidate entry'), and matching-context-types.ts:19. Cost: three correlated subqueries plus a `_canonical_counterparty` call and up to three `_bank_desc_word_match` calls per approved entry, on EVERY line click, growing with the client's whole booking history on that COA rather than with the offerable set. The face silently drops the surplus (matching-candidates.tsx:80-84 builds a Map keyed by entry_id and only reads `basisFor.get(c.entry_id)`), so nothing fails loudly — which is why no cell caught it: p657.db.matching-context asserts the SHAPE of a basis row, never its cardinality.
findings.fix: Apply the same capacity predicate to the basis subquery (wrap it the way :352-353 wraps the candidate projection, or add `and (<debit_remaining> > 0 or <credit_remaining> > 0)` to the `where` at 0226:620-627), and add one assertion to p657.db.matching-context: `candidate_basis.map(b => b.entry_id).sort()` deep-equals `list_bank_match_candidates(...).map(c => c.entry_id).sort()` for the same client + bank account.

findings.what: p657.db.capacity-race's 'capacity never goes negative' pair of assertions is dead code — the `if (row)` guard is never true, because the entry under test has exactly zero remaining capacity by the end of the cell and the recut read excludes zero-capacity candidates by construction.
findings.evidence: The cell gives ONE entry 90_000 of debit capacity on the bank COA (:265) and races two 90_000 lines at it; it then asserts at :328 that exactly 90_000 was consumed, i.e. debit_remaining is 0 and the entry carries no credit movement so credit_remaining is 0 too. 0226:352-353 filters the recut `list_bank_match_candidates` to rows with `debit_remaining_cents > 0 or credit_remaining_cents > 0`, and the sibling cell asserts that very exclusion at :379 ('a candidate with zero remaining capacity is absent from the read'). So `cands.find((c) => c.entry_id === entry)` at :320 is always `undefined`, `if (row)` at :321 is always false, and the two `assert.ok(... >= 0)` at :322-323 never execute. This is the review lens's textbook `if (rows.length) assert(...)` shape: the cell's stated third claim ('capacity never goes negative') is carried by nothing. The other two claims in the cell (blocking is observed through a real gate at :300-308; the refusal names reason/side/entry at :313-316) are genuine and were not touched by this finding.
findings.fix: Read the post-state capacity from the source of truth instead of from a read that hides spent entries — e.g. `select coalesce(sum(jl.debit_cents),0) - coalesce(sum(em.matched_cents),0)` against the entry, or assert on clara._bank_entry_side_capacity(entry, coa) — and drop the `if (row)` guard so the assertion cannot silently not run.

findings.what: The tail's item 9 is headed 'NO NEW TABLE, NO NEW EVENT TYPE, NO NEW accounting_work purpose (D14)' but asserts none of those three things — it asserts that every pre-existing `bank.%` event type has a trigger_taxonomy row, a fact about the estate that 0226 cannot move in either direction.
findings.evidence: The block is `select count(*) from clara.event_types where name like 'bank.%' and name not in (select event_type from clara.trigger_taxonomy)` with `if v_n <> 0 then raise`. MEASURED on clara_657: orphan count 0, `bank.%` event types 18, trigger_taxonomy 150 rows with 0 NULL event_type (so it is not additionally NULL-vacuous under `not in`, which was the other hazard). Nothing here counts tables, counts columns, or reads `accounting_work.purpose`'s IN-list at 0195:1711 — the migration could have created a table or widened the purpose list and this assertion would still print OK. It is the one item in an otherwise strong tail (items 1-8 are real and executable) whose stated claim and its measurement do not meet. The prose notice at :1109 repeats the tail's claims and does not mention item 9's subject, so the mismatch is confined to the comment.
findings.fix: Either assert the three things named — a `pg_class` count for the clara schema unchanged against a pinned number, and `position('accounting_work' in <this file's own text>) = 0` is not available so instead assert the purpose IN-list's cardinality at 0195:1711 is unchanged — or retitle the block to what it measures ('every bank.% event type still carries a taxonomy decision').

findings.what: The tail claims the thirteen cores' POST-IMAGE prosrc shas are asserted by p657.db.digest-census; that cell asserts no sha at all, and neither does anything else in the branch — so brief §3 item 5's 'asserting every post-image sha in the tail' is unmet and the tail points at evidence that does not exist.
findings.evidence: 0226:1073-1075 reads '(Post-image SHAs are asserted by the companion battery cell p657.db.digest-census, which measures them against the LIVE catalog rather than a transcription — see packages/db/tests/bank-line-existing-booking.test.mjs.)'. The cell contains no `sha256`, no `encode(`, no `digest(`: its per-core loop asserts only `src.includes("coalesce(clara._wake_task_id(), clara._bank_op_key_task(p_op_key))); -- H2, C2, #657")` and `src.includes("p_inputs_digest, p_op_key); -- H2, C2") === false`. The tail's own item 7 likewise counts a `prosrc like` match and asserts it equals 13. The thirteen shas exist ONLY as prose in reports/657-final.md's LOUD section, asserted by nothing. The substring assertions do carry the behavioural claim (a body either has the new call or it does not), so the risk is not that a core was missed — it is that the file states where its evidence lives and is wrong, which is exactly the class of claim AGENTS.md §6 forbids.
findings.fix: Either add the thirteen measured post-image shas as a pinned array in the tail (the 0195:390-409 idiom the prestate already uses), or correct the comment at :1073-1075 to say the post-image is proved by the counted anchor, not by a sha.

findings.what: The persistent outcome block does not render the receipt's operation key, although brief §3 web item 6 requires it and the component's own header says it does.
findings.evidence: brief-657.md §3 web item 6: 'a non-transient block naming the existing JE, the match allocation, the line, the receipt op key and the sentence "no new cash entry was created"'. matching-outcome.tsx:8 repeats it: '...the match allocation, the receipt's operation key, and the bank account.' The rendered `<dl>` at :61-80 carries outcomeMatchId, outcomeLines, outcomeEntries, outcomeAmount, outcomeAccountCode, outcomeCounterparty, outcomeSource — no op key. `grep -n "opKey" apps/web/components/bank/matching-outcome.tsx apps/web/components/bank/matching-outcome.test.tsx` returns nothing, and the only `opKeyLabel` in messages/en.json (:954) belongs to the Clara `bankAct` receipt part, a different namespace. Root cause: _match_bank_line_core's `_finish_op` payload (0226:715-735) does not echo p_op_key, so the receipt the face receives has no field to render — the door change and the face requirement were not reconciled. Consequence for AC10: a human who must quote 'the operation I already ran' to support has nothing on screen to quote.
findings.fix: Either add `'op_key', p_op_key` to the enriched _finish_op payload in 0226 §6 and render it as a new `<dt>/<dd>` pair (plus one ClientBank.matching key), or drop the claim from :8 and record the op key as a named residual in the report.

findings.what: Three orderings in the new read have no tiebreak, so two rows that agree on the sort key come back in an arbitrary order that a future test can pin on and then flake against.
findings.evidence: (a) `jsonb_agg(b.row_b order by b.posting_date desc)` at :570 — two candidate entries posted on the same date have no `, je.id` tiebreak, unlike the adjacent match_history projection which does carry one (`order by coalesce(bm.completed_at, bm.created_at) desc, bm.id desc`, :322). (b) and (c) `(select m.group_status from clara.bank_match_line_members m where m.line_id = l.id and m.group_status in ('pending','live') limit 1)` at :645-646 and the twin `match_id` subselect at :647-648 are `limit 1` with NO `order by`; the line-exclusivity index makes a second pending/live member row unlikely rather than impossible, and if one ever exists the two subselects can disagree with each other about WHICH match the line is on. Not measured as a live defect — no fixture on this rig produced a tie — which is why this is a note.
findings.fix: Add `, (b.row_b->>'entry_id')` to the basis aggregate's order, and collapse the two `limit 1` subselects into one `select ... into` with an explicit `order by` so they cannot name different rows.

findings.what: get_bank_line_matching_context does O(all statements on the account) + O(all approved bank-touching entries) work on every line click, and the surface calls it on every `?line=` change.
findings.evidence: At :546 it calls `clara.list_bank_statements(l.client_id, l.bank_account_id)` — which computes the header, lineage, `tie.gl_balance_cents` and `tie.unmatched_cents` for EVERY statement on that account (0038:7923-7957) — and then throws all but one away via the `jsonb_array_elements` filter at :547-549. The basis (see A2) then runs three correlated aggregate subqueries plus `_canonical_counterparty` and up to three `_bank_desc_word_match` calls per approved entry. apps/web/components/bank/matching-section.tsx:121-130 re-issues the read on every selectedLineId change (`useReloadOnChange` at :131). MEASURED payload on a 15-entry client: 3381 bytes, sub-second — so nothing is broken today; the shape is what scales badly, and #666/#667 land on this chassis next. `_bank_op_key_task` is additionally `IMMUTABLE` with a `SET search_path` clause, which blocks SQL inlining, but it is called once per receipt row so that is cosmetic.
findings.fix: Take the single statement's `tie` from a one-row call (or select the statement's own aggregates directly) instead of building every statement's tie and discarding them, and close A2 so the basis is bounded by the offerable candidate set.

findings.what: Four of the lens's highest-value targets were hunted and came back clean — recorded so the next reviewer does not re-spend the budget.
findings.evidence: CROSS-FIRM: get_bank_line_matching_context takes only p_line and is SECURITY DEFINER, so every table it touches was traced — bank_statement_lines `bl.firm_id = c.firm` (:534), bank_statements `bs.firm_id = c.firm` (:538), bank_accounts `a.firm_id = c.firm` (:542), bank_line_exceptions `e.firm_id = c.firm` (:561), journal_entries `je.firm_id = c.firm` (:620), documents `d.firm_id = c.firm` (:657), counterparties and bank_match_entry_members client-scoped via `l.client_id` (:606-610, :629). MEASURED: a firm-B persona reading a firm-A line returns `null`, the same answer a non-existent line returns — no existence oracle, exactly as the header at :507-509 claims. ARG-ORDER UNDER ONE KEY: the client sorts lineIds/entries before hashing (match-opkey.ts:50-56) while the door receives the raw arrays, so I raced the same key with the arrays reversed — MEASURED ok on both submissions, so _match_bank_line_core normalises before `_reserve_op` hashes and the sorted client key cannot manufacture an 'op_key reused with different args' CLR10. DISPATCH ORDER: handleP657Supabase is at serve-built.mjs:704, handleHomeBoardSupabase at :736 — above the EMPTY_RPCS arm as DECISIONS §6.1 requires, with a comment at both sites, and no SHARED_RPC_VERBS row was added. TASK BINDING: on clara_657, bank_agent_receipts holds 55 rows / 29 with wake_task_id, and the g1-written rows carry `wake_task_id` equal to field 2 of their own op_key (e.g. op_key `bank-pack:df74e400-...`, wake_task_id `df74e400-...`), so the stored column and the key-derived fallback agree on the live lane and the coalesce pair in _agent_verify_inputs_digest cannot disagree with itself there; the one row whose field 2 is not a uuid is the battery's own labelled fixture INSERT (p657.db.opkey-parse-free), not a real lane.
findings.fix: No change. Recorded as coverage, not as a defect.
